Many of tonight's ACL 2026 papers turned out to be unusually central to this topic —
titles like "The Evolution of Thought: Tracking LLM Overthinking via Reasoning Dynamics
Analysis," "Stop When Enough," "FoE: Forest of Errors," and "REST: Stress Testing Large
Reasoning Models" gave mechanistic accounts (reasoning-completion points, error-forest
propagation, attention drift toward a model's own prior reasoning) rather than just
another length-penalty variant. One paper (PaCoRe) is a useful counterweight: it scales
test-time compute to ~2M tokens per problem and gets real gains, which only makes sense
once its finding about "Reasoning Solipsism" is read alongside the skeptical papers —
naive parallel exploration fails for the same reason self-revision does elsewhere in this
archive; trained synthesis is what changes that.

adding another length-penalty variant: "Think Better, Not Longer" and
"AttnPO" both find a small, identifiable subset of a reasoning trace (marginal-
utility tokens; attention-selected "Key-Focus Heads") that already distinguishes
essential from redundant steps, without external supervision. "MathIF" is the
sharpest complication of the archive's usual framing — it shows longer or
reasoning-oriented-trained chain-of-thought measurably degrades instruction-
following, a cost of "more thinking" distinct from the accuracy plateau most
papers here track, and traces it to the instruction's growing contextual
distance from the final answer. "Programming over Thinking" (SCOPE) and
"Thermometer of Thoughts" both sidestep the length question by changing what
gets scaled instead — compiled solver code, and attention temperature rather
than the output distribution — and "Thinking-Based Non-Thinking" names reward
hacking as a specific way naive think/no-think RL training can be gamed, which
is a caution for any length-penalty design in this archive that hinges on
mode classification. A few papers were flagged plainly off-topic (a
psycholinguistics working-memory study, a legal-reasoning-trace benchmark, a
long-context sparse-attention paper matched only on the term "early stopping")
rather than forced into a fit.
